questiontext.text: The symmetry group of the square (D4) has how many elements?

feedback.text: Correct — 4 rotations and 4 reflections.

generalfeedback.text: The dihedral group D4 of the square has order 8: four rotations plus four reflections.

questiontext.text: Which set of rotations belongs to the square's symmetry group?

feedback.text: Correct — the four rotational symmetries of a square.
90 and 270 are also symmetries of the square.

generalfeedback.text: A square is invariant under rotations by 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees.

questiontext.text: Applying a D4 symmetry to a magic square produces...

feedback.text: Correct — rotations and reflections preserve the magic property.

answer.text: a square that is never magic

feedback.text: Symmetries map magic squares to magic squares.

generalfeedback.text: Each of the 8 symmetries permutes cells so that all line sums are preserved, giving another magic square.

questiontext.text: How many reflection symmetries does the square (D4) have?

feedback.text: Correct — two through edge midpoints and two through diagonals.
There are four reflection axes, not two.
8 is the total group order; reflections number 4.
The square does have reflection symmetries.

generalfeedback.text: D4 has 4 reflection axes: two diagonal and two through opposite edge midpoints.

questiontext.text: The square's symmetry group D4 has order 8, made of 4 rotations and 4 reflections.

feedback.text: Correct — 4 + 4 = 8 symmetries.
D4 indeed has 8 elements: 4 rotations and 4 reflections.

Correct — rotation maps a magic square to another magic square.
